atlas-sg.0066: GovTech, the government’s technology agency, is among the top IT graduate employers, with internships, a Smart Nation scholarship and a Technology Associate Programme.
atlas-sg.0067: 88.9% of the autonomous universities’ 2025 graduates had a job within six months, at a median of S$4,500 a month. Foreign graduates still need an Employment Pass above the salary floor.
atlas-sg.0068: Information and digital technologies graduates had the highest median pay of any cluster in the 2025 survey, S$5,500 a month.
atlas-sg.0069: AI Singapore’s AI Apprenticeship Programme trains engineers on real projects and says over 90% of its graduates are hired, by DSTA, DBS, Grab, Capgemini and AI Singapore itself; Parliament has asked how many stay in-house.
atlas-sg.0070: COMPASS gives more points for a degree from a listed top-tier institution: NUS, NTU, SMU and a list of foreign universities and faculties.
atlas-sg.0071: In the points test, qualifications score 20 points for a top-tier institution and 10 for another degree-equivalent qualification, and verification proof is needed only if you claim those points; in hiring, EY took roughly 75% of its graduates from the autonomous universities.
atlas-sg.0072: NTU’s flagship career fair runs each September and February, and SMU holds its Career Fair twice a year with over 100 companies; the postgraduate fair at SMU, for students with more than two years of work experience, took place in February 2026.
atlas-sg.0073: Bank programmes start in July after a selection that runs from the previous autumn: DBS commences on 5 July 2027 and HSBC’s assessment centres run from September to November 2026; NTU’s main fair repeats in September and February.
atlas-sg.0074: The programme pages read ask for recent graduates, not a master’s: HSBC wants a GPA of at least 4.0 out of 5.0 (or 3.2 out of 4.0) and graduation by July 2027 or under 2 years of full-time experience.
atlas-sg.0075: For a work pass, MOM wants proof that qualifications are authentic and awarded by accredited institutions, through an MOM-listed background screening company or a verifiable awarding-institution portal; plain certificates and notarised copies are not accepted.
atlas-sg.0076: School name counts twice: COMPASS gives 20 points to a top-tier institution against 10 for another degree, and EY took roughly 75% of its graduates from the autonomous universities while PwC recruits mostly from local universities.
atlas-sg.0077: None of the graduate programmes read is a dual-study scheme: the routes are internships, management-associate programmes and a few apprenticeship-style schemes such as AI Singapore’s and OCBC Ignite.
atlas-sg.0078: The Ministry of Education ranked 2nd and the Monetary Authority of Singapore 56th in gradsingapore’s 2026 list of leading graduate employers, and the Public Service Commission offers scholarships that lead into the Public Service.
atlas-sg.0079: Over 80% of the financial-sector workforce is local and more than 9 in 10 net new jobs in 2018 to 2023 went to locals; an Employment Pass needs S$5,600 a month (S$6,200 in finance), 40 COMPASS points and a 14-day MyCareersFuture advert. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-sg.0080: A photo is not legally required but is common in Singapore, especially for entry-level or government roles; use a clean formal headshot, and only if the employer asks or it is the convention for the role.
atlas-sg.0081: Entry-level candidates and fresh graduates should aim for one to two pages; two to three pages are typical at mid-level.
atlas-sg.0082: The programme pages read (DBS, UOB, HSBC) describe an online application followed by assessments and interviews and do not ask for a cover letter; add one when a posting requests it.
atlas-sg.0083: Prepare a separate reference list only when the employer asks; get each referee’s permission first and do not publish their contact details in your resume.
atlas-sg.0084: Graduate applications ask for results rather than certified copies (HSBC sets a GPA minimum); certified proof comes later, at the work-pass stage, where MOM does not accept plain certificates and wants verified proof, with an English translation for non-English documents.
atlas-sg.0085: Employers publish bands: a MyCareersFuture advert used for an Employment Pass must show the salary range, and the maximum cannot exceed twice the minimum.
atlas-sg.0086: Qualification checks are routine at the pass stage: employers must ensure candidates’ qualifications are authentic and awarded by accredited institutions, and verification is needed once per candidate.
atlas-sg.0087: Hiring is public by design for foreign hires: the job must be advertised on MyCareersFuture for 14 consecutive days without an offer being made, and the MOM page warns against pre-selecting a foreigner and advertising only for show.
atlas-sg.0088: A foreign graduate needs an employer willing to apply for a pass and pay above the floor: S$5,600 a month today (S$6,200 in finance), 40 COMPASS points, and candidates below the salary are ineligible whatever their points.
atlas-sg.0089: English. Work-pass documents not in English must be uploaded with an English translation, and the programme pages read are in English.
atlas-sg.0090: Bank selection mixes online applications, assessments and a long day: DBS’s Management Associate selection ends in a full-day Case Challenge with case work and group exercises, and HSBC runs in-person or virtual assessment centres from September to November.
atlas-sg.0091: Recruitment is rolling at some banks, so applications may close early: HSBC’s listing shows closing dates of 31 August and 30 October 2026 on the same page.
atlas-sg.0092: Big Four graduate hiring is high-volume: PwC drew more than 2,000 applications a cycle for a class of over 250.
atlas-sg.0093: Employers must give key employment terms in writing, including the probation and notice periods; if the contract names no notice, the default is 1 day under 26 weeks of service, 1 week up to 2 years, 2 weeks up to 5 years and 4 weeks beyond.
atlas-sg.0094: Programme pay is a band shown in the advert, such as DBS’s 12-month permanent Analyst post, so there is little room to negotiate; starting pay is about S$4,300 at EY and from S$4,350 at PwC.
atlas-sg.0095: The employer must clear the Fair Consideration Framework first: advertise on MyCareersFuture for at least 14 consecutive days and make no offer in that period, unless exempt (fewer than 10 employees, a fixed monthly salary of S$22,500 or more, a role of one month or less, or an intra-company transfer).
atlas-sg.0096: Then the pass: the salary must clear S$5,600 a month (S$6,200 in finance) before COMPASS is even scored, and COMPASS needs 40 points from salary, qualifications, nationality diversity, local-employment support and bonuses.
atlas-sg.0097: Ask early whether the employer sponsors and at what level: over 80% of finance staff are local, and a starting salary of about S$4,000 to 4,500 sits below the floor, which is why this works mostly in finance, tech and consulting.
atlas-sg.0098: Portals: MyCareersFuture, the government job portal, and the employers’ own pages (DBS, UOB, HSBC, GovTech); gradsingapore publishes the ranking of leading graduate employers.
atlas-sg.0099: Campus: NTU’s career fair in September and February, SMU’s Career Fair twice a year, both through the universities’ career offices.
atlas-sg.0100: Public sector: scholarships.gov.sg lists the PSC and agency scholarships, and GovTech’s student and graduate page lists internships and its Technology Associate Programme.
atlas-sg.0101: Applying late to the July bank cohorts: HSBC’s assessment centres run from September to November 2026 for a July 2027 start and recruitment is rolling, so the window can close early.
atlas-sg.0102: Ignoring the salary floor: an Employment Pass needs S$5,600 a month (S$6,200 in finance), rising from 1 January 2027, and a candidate under the floor is ineligible whatever the COMPASS score.
atlas-sg.0103: Sending unverifiable qualifications: MOM does not accept plain certificates or notarised copies as proof, and screenshots from sources it cannot verify are rejected.
atlas-sg.0104: A CV that is too long: fresh graduates should aim for one to two pages, and Jobstreet suggests leaving out age, religion and marital status.
atlas-sg.0105: The bank programmes read (DBS, UOB, HSBC) are run and advertised in English; the pages state no other language requirement.
atlas-sg.0106: The Big Four graduate classes in Singapore are described in English-language reporting, and the pages read state no language test.
atlas-sg.0107: GovTech’s student and graduate programmes are described in English with no stated language test; PSC scholarships lead into the Public Service.
atlas-sg.0108: GovTech and AI Singapore run their technology programmes in English.
atlas-sg.0109: AI Singapore’s AI Apprenticeship Programme is described in English and places graduates with DSTA, DBS, Grab and Capgemini.
atlas-sg.0110: In the 2025 graduate survey of the six autonomous universities, 88.9% had secured employment within six months, 83.4% were employed, 74.4% were in full-time permanent jobs and the median gross monthly salary was S$4,500; business graduates had 91.2% secured employment and a median of S$4,400.
atlas-sg.0111: The survey covers graduates of local universities; international students on a student pass need an employer to apply for a pass, and no source read reports outcomes for them separately.
atlas-sg.0113: The university registers you on SOLAR, you file the eForm 16 two to three months before term and receive an in-principle approval to travel; stays of six months or more need a medical.
atlas-sg.0114: Students at public universities (NUS, NTU, SMU and others, INSEAD and ESSEC included) may work 16 hours a week in term; students at private schools may not work at all.
